slides.title: CSMA/CD
slides.body:
Step By Step - Process
If a mismatch is detected → collision → send a jam signal to alert all devices → stop transmitting
If the transmitted signal matches what is received → no collision → continue
Transmitting Data

slides.title: CSMA/CD
slides.body:
Step By Step - Process
Wait a random back-off time (Binary Exponential Backoff) → try again
Re-Transmission
Waits

slides.title: CSMA/CD
slides.body:
Binary Exponential Backoff
After 1st collision 
Wait random time from {0 , 1} slot times
After 2nd collision 
Wait random time from {0, 1, 2, 3} slot times
After kth collision 
Wait random time from {0, 1, ..., 2^k - 1} slot times
After 16 collisions 
Abort transmission and report failure

slides.title: CSMA/CD
slides.body:
Analogy
Analogy: CSMA/CD is like speaking in a conference call. You talk, and also listen to what is coming back. If you hear two voices mixed together (including yours), you know there is a collision — you stop, say 'sorry, you go ahead,' wait a random time, and try again

slides.title: Ethernet Frame Format
slides.body:
Minimum frame size: 64 bytes (excluding Preamble and SFD)
Maximum frame size: 1518 bytes (excluding Preamble and SFD)
MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) = 1500 bytes (maximum data/payload inside the frame)
If data < 46 bytes, padding is added to reach the minimum
Reason for Minimum Size: Ensure collision detection works properly on longest cable runs
Frame Size Rules

slides.title: Ethernet Frame Format
slides.body:
Recipient’s Address (Destination MAC)
Return Address (Source MAC)
Customs Declaration (Type/Length)
Letter Inside → Data (Payload)
Tamper Seal → CRC (Error Check)
Analogy
tables:
🎯 Analogy
An Ethernet frame is like a formal letter sent through courier. The envelope has: the recipient's address (Destination MAC), your return address (Source MAC), a customs declaration of contents (Type/Length), the actual letter inside (Data), and a tamper-seal (CRC). If the seal is broken on arrival, the letter is rejected — just like a corrupted frame is discarded.

slides.title: Switches
slides.body:
Intelligent Frame Forwarding
A Switch is a multi-port device that creates a dedicated path between sender and receiver, eliminating collisions on all ports

slides.title: Switches
slides.body:
How a Switch Works?
Source MAC
Switch learns the Source MAC and stores it in the MAC Address Table
Destination MAC
Switch checks if the Destination MAC is in the table
Found: Forward to specific port
Not Found: Flood to all ports except source port
Learning
Over time, the table grows, forwarding frames efficiently

Each port is its own domain, no CSMA/CD
